INTRODUCTION 
            I, the Chairman, Standing Committee on Transport and Tourism, having been authorised by the Committee to
 present on their behalf, present this Thirty-ninth Report on the Demands for Grants 1999-2000 of the Ministry of
 Surface Transport.           
2.         The Committee at its meeting held on 26
th & 30th March,1999, considered the Demands for Grants 1999-2000
 of the Ministry of Surface Transport (Demand Nos. 78, 79 and 80) and heard the Secretary, the Ministry of Surface
 Transport on the subject. 
3.         The Committee expresses its thanks to the officers of the Ministry for placing before the Committee, the material
 and information desired in connection with the examination of the Demands for Grants of the Ministry and for giving
 evidence before the Committee. 
4.         The Committee considered and adopted the Report at its meeting held on the 8
th April, 1999.
 
 
New Delhi                                                                                                    
 PROF. VIJAY KUMAR MALHOTRA
8TH April,1999                                                                                                                 Chairman
Chaitra 18,1921(Saka)                                                                               Committee on Transport &Tourism
           
 
REPORT 
 
The Ministry of Surface Transport is responsible for the development, formulation and implementation of policies on
 road transport and inland water transport, development and modernisation of major ports, lighthouses and lightships,
 shipbuilding industries, Central Sector Road Schemes, administration of Central Road Fund and Co-ordination of
 research pertaining to road works.  Besides, the Ministry is responsible for making necessary shipment arrangements by
 chartering ships at economic and competitive rates in respect of Government owned/controlled bulk carriers.  
2.         The Ministry is administratively divided into different wings, namely roads, Ports, shipping, Road Transport,
 Chartering development and finance.
3.         The following are the subordinate offices, public sector undertakings and autonomous bodies functioning under
 the administrative control of this Ministry:-
 
SUBORDINATE OFFICES: 
1.         Directorate General of Shipping
2.         Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships
3.         Andaman and Lakshadweep Harbour Works
4.         Minor Ports Survey Organisations.
 
AUTONOMOUS  BODIES:
 
1.         Port Trust at Mumbai, Calcutta, Cochin, Kandla, Madras, Murmugao, New Mangalore, Jawaharlal Nehru Port
 Trust, Paradip, Tuticorin and Vishakhapatnam.
2.         Inland Waterways Authority of India
3.         National Highways Authority of India
4.         National Ship Design and Research Centre at Vishakhapatnam
5.         Dock Labour Boards at Mumbai, Calcutta, Cochin, Kandla, Madras, Murmugao and Vishakhapatnam
6.         National Institute of Training of Highway Engineers.
 
PUBLIC SECTOR UNDERTAKINGS
 
1.         Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Limited
2.         Shipping Corporation of India Limited

            The following three demands pertain to the Ministry of Surface Transport:
(a)        Demand No. 78: Surface Transport
(b)        Demand No. 79: Roads and
(c)        Demand No. 80: Ports, Light houses and shipping.
 
DEMAND No. 78: SURFACE TRANSORT
 
4.         This demand covers the activities related to the surface transport sector i.e. (I) road transport sector for 
 formulation of broad policies concerning road transport, motor vehicle legislation, legislation related to State Road
 Transport Corporations and movement of vehicular traffic with neighboring countries and (ii) inland water transport
 sector. Under this demand a provision of Rs. 86.39 crores has been kept for the year 1999-2000 as against Rs. 121.40
 crores at the B.E. and Rs. 100.62 crores at the R.E. stages for the year 1998-99.
 
(i)         Road Transport Sector
5.         The 8
th plan outlay for road transport sector was Rs. 264 crores. However the 9th plan outlay for this sector is
 only Rs. 77.15 crores.    The Committee was informed the reasons for this huge gap is that the working group on VIII
 plan recommended Rs. 766 crores for road transport sector.  However, allocation was made to the tune of Rs. 264
 crores only which included an allocation of Rs. 140 crores for DTC.  The working group on road transport for the 9th 
 plan recommended an outlay of Rs. 328 crores for this sector, however, the planning commission has approved an
 outlay of Rs. 77 crores. The annual plan for 1999-2000 provides for Rs. 9 crores.
 
6.         The Committee was very much surprised to know that the budgetary allocation for this important sector
 relating to road transport, which covers matters relating to road safety, control of vehicular pollution, accidents
 on roads etc., which directly effects public life, has not only been reduced for the year 1998-99 but a lesser
 amount provided during 1999=2000. The total 9th plan allocation is only Rs. 77.15 crores against Rs. 378 crores
 recommended by the working group on road transport sector as compared to Rs. 264 crores during 8th plan.
 The Committee is of the opinion that keeping in view the high rate of accidents on Indian roads and the existing
 levels of pollution especially in the metropolitan cities, this sector deserves higher allocations which would go a
 long way in making the driving safer on the Indian roads as well as for providing clean environment in the cities.
 
ROAD SAFETY AND VEHICULAR POLLUTION 
7.         The Committee was informed that there are miscellaneous schemes pertaining to road transport sector.  These
 basically comprise of Road safety programmes.  The assistance is provided in the form of grants-in-aid to various State
 Governments.  The grants-in-aid is given for taking up proposals relating  to National Highways Patrolling scheme and
 scheme for Pollution Testing Equipments.
 
8.         During the year 1998-99 a total provision of Rs. 13.00 crores was made for taking up various road safety
 programmes.  Out of these Rs. 13 crores, Rs. 4 crores was for grants-in-aid to State governments and Rs. 9 crores for
 other road safety programmes such as publicity measures on road safety.  Training of drivers in unorganised sector,
 study on transport industry, strengthening of Central Institute of Road Transport (CIRT), Pune and Research &
 Development Schemes etc.  At R.E. stage, these provisions have been reduced to Rs. 2.77 crores and Rs. 2.73 crores
 respectively.
 
9.         For 1999-2000 a provisions of Rs. 9 crores has been made in the plan budget.  Out of this Rs. 4.00 crores
 provisions has been made for grant-in-aid to State governments and two schemes viz. National Highway patrolling
 schemes an amount of Rs. 3 crores and Pollution Testing Equipments an amount of Rs. 1 crore have been kept Rs. 4.00
 crores has been provided for other road safety programmes such as publicity measures on Road Safety, Training of 
 Drivers in unorganised sector, study on Transport Industry, strengthening of CIRT Pune and R & D scheme etc.

10.       The Committee was unhappy to note that despite its recommendation as contained in its 33rd Report for
 enhanced budgetary allocation for road safety measures, no action appears to have been taken by the Ministry
 to increase the amount for the said purpose and instead only Rs. 1 Crore has been provided whereas Rs. 2.5
 crores was the budgetary allocation during the year 1998-99.  The Committee further observed that with this
 meager allocation it would not be possible for the Ministry to cover all the States. The Committee, therefore,
 reiterates its earlier recommendation that amount for the purpose should be increased in order to give wide
 publicity to various road safety measures, so that the number of road accidents which are increasing day by day
 could be reduced.  The Committee further recommends that a Centrally sponsored scheme should be introduced
 for this purpose so that more and more States could enjoy the benefits of it in order to make transport system of
 their States more safer and pollution free.
 
STATE ROAD TRANSPORT CORPORATIONS
11.       The 9
th plan outlay for capital contribution to the SRTCs is Rs. 20 crores.  This scheme was dispensed with from
 the year 1993-94.  Provisions in the budget were being made to liquidate the arrears.
 
12.       The annual plan outlay under this head during 1998-99 was Rs. 3.00 crores which was reduced to Rs. 1.6 crores
 at R.E. stage.  Out of this Rs. 1.517 crores has been released to Gujarat SRTC.  The Committee was informed that many
 of the State Governments have requested for the revival of the scheme.  Realizing the need for revival of this scheme,
 the matter was taken up by the Ministry of Surface Transport with Planning Commission.  The working group on road
 transport has suggested the following criteria for granting capital contribution to SRTCs. The share of capital
 contribution for purchase of buses should be kept in the ratio of 1:2. Wherein one part i.e. 33% would be provided by
 the Central  Government and the balance 67% will have be provided for by State Governments.  In case the SRTCs
 were able to raise funds from the financing agencies, the need for getting the financial support from the State
 Government could be dispensed with.
 
13.       The Committee was informed that the above formulation which was referred to Planning Commission for
 concurrence has been rejected by it. The Committee, however, realises the need for revival of this scheme as assistance
 to SRTC’s is essential in view of the fact that their services are largely used by common man. The Committee desires
 that reasons for discontinuing the scheme may be furnished to it. However, the Committee observed that many
 States have requested for revival of the scheme, it would be appropriate if such a scheme may be revived
 especially  for the benefit of those States which are totally dependent on road transport. The Committee also
 desires that funds should be provided to those corporations, which could improve their performance if financial
 support is extended to them.
 
 (ii)       INLAND WATER TRANSPORT SECTOR
14.       The 9
th plan outlay for the Inland Water Transport sector is Rs. 408 crores.  During 1999-2000, the plan outlay
 for IWT sector is Rs. 26.04 crores consisting of Rs. 6.04 crores for Central Inland Water Transport Corporation
 (CIWTC), Rs. 20.00 crores for Inland Waterway Authority of India (IWAI) which includes Grants to Inland Waterways
 Authority of India and for other schemes such as Technical studies, research and development schemes for IWT
 personnel, interest subsidy to bank/financial institutions for loans to IWT entrepreneurs and other incentive schemes.
 
15.       During 1998-99 Ministry of Surface Transport projected fund requirement of Rs. 143.70 crores against which
 budgetary allocation made was Rs. 45.00 crores at B.E. stage which was reduced to Rs. 33.91 crores at R.E. state.  The
 amount allocated at R.E. stage was utilised fully.
 
16.       The Committee was informed that for the year 1999-2000 the Ministry of Surface Transport has projected fund
 requirement of Rs. 129.37 crores, but the budgetary allocation has been made only for Rs. 20 crores for IWAI.  This
 drastic reduction is not sufficient even to meet the requirement for the schemes which are under execution.  The IWAI
 has requested for enhancement in B.E. 1999-2000.  The Ministry of Surface Transport requested Planning Commission
 to consider enhanced allocation because in case the allocations during 1999-2000 are not increased, it  will result in set
 back in achieving the target set for the 9
th plan by the Government for IWT sector. The three waterways which are
 covered under this sector are:-

(A)    National Waterways No.1
17.       Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system from Allahabad to Haldia ( 1620 kms.) was declared as National
 Waterway  in 1986.  The waterway  is being developed for shipping and navigation and infrastructure facilities such as
 fairway terminals and Navigational aids are provided.  Loading/unloading/terminal facilities are existing at Haldia,
 Calcutta, Pakur, Farakka, Bhagalpur,Munger , Patna, Ballia and Varanasi. Public sector CIWTC and private operators
 operate vessels between Haldia and Varanasi. A provision of Rs. 5 crores has been made  during 9
th plan for setting up
 of terminals, Rs.15 crores for terminal at Gaighat, at Patna and  Rs. 3 crores for infrastructural facilities  between Patna
 and Allahabad, apart from other miscellaneous works.
 
(B)       National Waterway NO.2
18.       The river Brahmaputra from Dhubri to Sadiya (891 Kms) was declared as National waterway No. 2 in 1988.
 This  waterways runs through  Bangaladesh and Sunderbans and  links North-East part of the country with the ports of
 Calcutta and Haldia and is a very important traditional IWT route. Under an agreement with the Government of
 Bangaladesh , the CIWTC and other Indian  vessels operators ply cargo between Assam and Calcutta region making
 use of IWT transit facilities through Bangaladesh. Floating terminal facilities have been provided at Dhubri , Jogighopa
 ,Pandu, Tejpur, and Neamati and at Sadiya and Saikhowoa similar facilities would be provided during 1999-2000. A
 provision Rs.  5 crores exists for terminals during 9
th plan, Rs. 10 crores for 24 hours navigational aids, Rs. 10 crores
 for fairway improvement/conservancy  works, Rs. 4 crores for terminal maintenance, 15 crores for acquisition of
 dredgers and allied vessels and Rs. 4 crores for acquisition/replacement of survey vessels, apart from other
 miscellaneous works. 
 
(C)       National waterway No.3
19.       The West-Coast canal from Kottapuram to Kollam alongwith Champakara and Udyogamandal canals (205 Kms)
 was declared as National waterway No. 3 in 1993. The waterway composes of natural lakes, back-waters, river sections
 and manmade canal sections. The cargo handling terminal exist at Kochi port, Udyogamandal, Ambalamugal, and
 Edapallikota etc. A provision of Rs. 2 crores exists for construction and maintenance of locks, Rs. 8 crores for land
 acquisition for construction of terminals, Rs. 27 crores for capital dredging ,Rs. 1 crores for acquisition survey vessels
 and Rs. 3.21 crores for 24 hours navigational aids, apart from other miscellaneous works exists for 9
th plan period.
 
20.       A provision of Rs. 10 crores exist for development of new waterways under 9
th plan. Such waterways are,
 Sunderbans, Godavari river, Goa rivers, Bangladesh protocal routes, East Coast canal, Mahanadi and Brahmani rivers,
 Narmada river, extension of NW-3 in North and South sides, DVC canal, river Yamuna in Delhi region, Kakinada,
 Mercunam canal and Barak river.
 
21.       The Committee was informed that during first two years of 9
th plan there were drastic reductions both at BE and
 RE stages which have led to slowing down of development works for IWT sector. However, many important schemes
 for infrastructure development on three national water ways have been initiated during the first two years of 9
th plan.
 Some of these schemes are capital dredging including land acquisition for widening for narrow sections of canal in
 NW-3, procurement of hydraulic surface dredges for NW-1 and 2 and land acquisition for construction of terminal on
 NW-3, provision of 24  hrs navigational aids on certain stretches of NW-1 and NW-2, acquisition of survey launches
 for NW-2 and NW-3, permanent RCC hardware and software for hydrographic survey system etc.
 
22.       The Committee noted with concern the less budgetary allocations made in respect of IWT sector despite its
 earlier recommendations in previous reports to increase budgetary allocations to this sector. The reduced allocations
 are  inadequate to meet the targets for the development of IWT. The Committee feels that the development of
 waterways in the country which were contemplated to the share some of the load from the road/rail sector, is very slow
 due to shortage of funds and improper planning. The Committee was informed that this mode of transport is more cost-
effective than road sector. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Public Sector Undertakings may be asked to
 earmark some percentage of their Cargo for water transport sector. The Committee, further, recommends that the
 Ministry should take up the matter with regard to less allocation of grants to this sector  with the Planning Commission
 more seriously and it should be specifically underlined to the Planning Commission the significance of this important

 transport sector,  which would, if developed in time, not only lessen the burden on the road/rail sectors but also is a
 much cleaner and less polluting mode of transportation.  They may also be apprised that  the projects under IWT sector
 are moving at a snail’s pace and in order to ensure that these are completed in time without further cost overruns,  it is
 necessary that adequate allocations should be made for water transport sector.  The Committee also observed that in our
 country the IWT sector has been neglected for a long time and if the same attitude continues towards such a nature
 friendly transportation system, definitely the IWT sector will not survive. The Committee also desired that a total
 review of the IWT sector is required and suggests that both the Ministry of Surface Transport and Planning
 Commission take a realistic view and prepare such a plan so as to make a better use of this mode of transportation.
 
 
CENTRAL INLAND WATER TRANSPORT CORPORATION
23.       In 9
th five year plan, a tentative allocation of Rs. 100 crores has been made for various schemes of CIWTC.
 Budget allocation of Rs. 15.04 crores for plan schemes was provided in the financial year 1998-99 which was reduced
 to Rs. 7.30 crores at RE stage. For the financial year 1999-2000, against a demand of Rs. 10.16 crores, only Rs. 6.04
 crores has been provided. It was pointed out to the Committee  that  sufficient allocation in favour of CIWTC for its
 various schemes including repair/replacement of overage vessels, capital repair of minor terminals, modernisation of
 handling facilities of minor terminals etc., has not been provided. The Committee was also informed that CIWTC has
 incurred accumulated losses amounting for Rs. 140 crores till date.   
 
24.       The non-plan provision in BE for the year 1999-2000 for CIWTC was Rs. 8 crores. However, due to the fact that
 the deficit of the company was increasing and statutory payments had to be made, the non-plan support to CIWTC was
 increased from Rs. 8 crores to Rs. 12.05 crores in RE stage during last year. But for BE 1999-2000 a provisions of Rs.
 9.56 crores only has been made but in view of the precarious financial position of the company a minimum support of
 atleast Rs.16 crores is required. The revival package of the company is under consideration of the Cabinet. Thus non-
plan outlay of Rs. 9.56 crores for first 6 month has been acquired pending cabinet decision.
 
25.       The Committee finds that no serious attempt is being made by the Ministry of Surface Transport to turn around
 CIWTC which has been incurring losses since its inception despite its earlier recommendation as contained in its 33
rd
 report for early restructuring of the Company to that fact. The Committee, therefore, impresses upon the Ministry of
 Surface Transport to take an early decision with regard to the restructuring of CIWTC which would also give
 boost to the growth and development of IWT sector in the country.
 
DEMAND NO.79
26.       This demand covers the activities related to the construction, development and maintenance of National
 Highways, strategic and border roads, inter state roads, permanent bridges and roads of economic importance, schemes
 financed under the Central Road Fund, Bridges fees fund etc. The total amount allocated under this demand for 1999-
2000 is Rs. 3,709.54 crores against Rs. 3,431.12 crores at BE stage which was reduced to Rs. 2865.11 crores at R.E.
 stage for the year 1998-99.
 
NATIONAL HIGHWAYS
27.       National Highways consisting of 35610 Kms. constituted about 1.7% of the length of entire road net work in the
 country but carry about 40% of total road traffic. In the 8
th plan, the provision for roads sector was Rs. 2600 crores,
 against the projected requirements of about Rs. 23,000 crores, the 9th plan outlay is restricted to Rs. 7929.04 crores. An
 estimated amount of Rs. 52,000 crores is needed only for removal of various existing deficiencies.
 
28.       During the first year of 9th plan total plan expenditure was Rs. 1565.31 crores. During 1999-2000 planning
 commission have allocated Rs. 2163.08 crores for the development of National Highways on plan side. Out of this Rs.
 819.87 is for externally aided schemes and Rs. 1343.21 crores is for other normal national highways.
 
29.       For the year 1999-2000 planning commission have allocated Rs. 1442.51 crores in non-plan side. This amount
 will be spent on Maintenance of National Highways.
 
30.       The Committee was informed that in conformity with the National Highways Act. 1988, the National Highway

 been included in BE for 1999-2000. The purpose of this investment is to enable NHAI to leverage resources from the

 31.      The Committee was informed that, with regard to normal National Highways, the requirement of funds for the
 year 1999-2000 for ongoing works has been estimated as Rs. 923 crores. In addition to this a sum of Rs. 300 crores
 may be required for the work sanctioned during last year. Thus the total requirement of funds for the normal ongoing
 works comes out to be Rs. 1223 crores. A sum of Rs. 691 crores is proposed to be spent on ongoing externally aided

Externally-aided-projects                              Rs.      1895.00 crores

32.       The Committee was also informed that the requirements for ongoing works has been reduced from Rs. 4878
 crores (as on 1.4.97) to Rs. 3118 crores (1.4.99).  Keeping in view the requirement of funds for completion of ongoing
 works expeditiously and  priority projects, the requirement of funds for National Highways amounts to Rs. 2500 crores
 for the year 1999-2000, but funds made available under NH’s is of the order of Rs.772.41 crores only.
 
33.       The Committee was informed that for speedy implementation of National Highways projects certain measure,
 like simplification of land, acquisition procedures, dispensing with procedures like clearance of M/0 Environment &
 Forest for projects relating to improvements of existing roads, fast approval of estimates have been approved by the
 cabinet. The Ministry has been given powers to give environment clearance. Govt. has accorded a high priority to
 infrastructure development including roads. More financial powers have also been delegated to M/o Surface Transport
 as a special case for National Highway projects.
 
34.       The Committee  noted with concern low funds being allocated for normal network of National Highways
 Schemes and the constraints in respect of generating funds for implementation of National Highways Schemes. The
 Committee also observed that the condition of National Highways in the country is bad and  is perturbed to note that
 slowly the National Highways are getting converted into intercity highways. The Committee also shows it concern to
 the fact that the entire network of National Highways is not under National Highways Authority of India and that only
 part of it is being maintained by NHAI and the rest is still being maintained by state PWD’s/BRO/BRDB which has
 resulted in the poor quality of National Highways especially those, which are under State PWD’s and other agencies as
 sufficient funds are not allotted for it and neither NHAI nor the Ministry of Surface Transport exercise any kind of
 control on these agencies.  There exists no machinery or system for regular monitoring with regard to the repairs being
 made on these National Highways. The Committee also found that the maintenance of  National Highways  is of sub-
standard quality.   
 
 
35.       The Committee, therefore, recommends that sufficient funds should be allotted for repair and maintenance of
 National Highways in the country and that the entire length of National Highways network should be brought under the
 NHAI. The Committee also desires that the entire administrative control over state PWD’s/BRO/BRDB should be with
 National Highways Authority of India in so far as it relating to the construction/maintenance of National Highways  and
 that  NHAI should establish a separate  machinery so as  to have a strict watch on the maintenance and repairs carried
 out by these agencies. The Committee further desires that the maintenance of National Highways should be as per
 defined standards.
 
36.       The Committee understands that a lot of unauthorised structures like restaurants, factories, dhabas, workshops
 have come up on both sides of many National Highways causing obstructions in the smooth flow of traffic. The
 Committee is of the view that for the smooth and unhindered flow of traffic, the National Highways should remain free
 from any type of encroachments.
 
NATIONAL HIGHWAYS DEVELOPMENT PROJECT

37.       The Committee was also apprised by the Ministry of Surface Transport/ National Highway Authority of India
 that as announced by the Prime Minister recently a programme regarding six laning of the North-South, East-West
 corridor connecting Kashmir to Kanyakumari and Silchar to Sourashtra in an aggregate length of 7000 Kms has been
 undertaken on priority basis. The linking of four major metropolitan cities connecting Delhi-Calcutta, Chennai and
 Mumbai with an aggregate length of about 4000 Kms.  known as Golden Quadrilateral has also been made part of the
 Prime Minister’s Scheme of East-West, South-North corridor by the Task Force appointed for the purpose under a
 single project to be termed as “National Highways Development Project”. The Task Force has decided that the project
 will be implemented by NHAI. 
 
38.       The funds requirement for the National  Highways Development Project is of the order of Rs. 50,000 crores, and
 in case  the  development of express ways is also  included, the requirement will go up to Rs. 1,24.000 crores.
              
39.       The Committee was apprised that the Ministry  has so far  identified, 9,400 Kms. of express ways network, 1400
 Kms. of 6 laning and 5500 Kms. of 4 laning to be developed over the next 10 to 15 years under the National Highway
 Development Project at a cost of Rs. 1,24,000 crores approximately. The development  needs of the remaining network
 of National Highways will also cost Rs. 1,26,000 crores approximately in addition to the amount for NHDP thus the
 total requirement of funds for the purpose will be of the order of Rs. 2,50,000 crores over the next 15 years.
 
40.       The Committee has been further  informed that the Task Force has finalised alignment of these corridors and the
 Ministry propose to commence construction work on at least 20 locations out of which work at one location at
 Devanahalli near  Bangalore  which measures about 265 Kms. has already been  started.
 
41.       The Committee was further informed that the project reports pertaining to the entire NHDP would only be
 completed by the 2001, however, some are expected to be finalised by the end of 1999 and some in the middle of the
 year 2000. After the completion of Project Reports bids will be prepared and issued for allotment of works. The entire
 process including preparation of project reports, issue of bids and allotment of works may only be completed by the
 year 2001 and the works relating to entire project is expected to be completed there after with next 5 years.
 
42.       The Committee noted the scheme announce by the Prime Minister regarding National Highway Development
 Project. The Committee is of the view that an in-depth study with regard to Golden Quadrilateral and construction of
 North-South, East-West corridor known as NHDP may be carried out immediately and the Committee should be
 informed about the total policy, time frame and financial implications involved in its implementation.
 
BORDER ROADS
43.       With a view to provide accessibility to far flung areas so as to bring them into the National mainstream, special
 programme of road construction in such areas was initiated by the Government. Various National Highways works in
 the States of Arunchal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland,
 Tripura, West Bengal, Bihar, Sikkim  and Uttar Pradesh were approved under this scheme. Some missing links in
 border areas  were also identified to be taken up under this scheme. The amount of Rs. 103.00 crores have been
 provided during 1999-2000. These works are being executed by the Border Roads Development Board. There is a dire
 need for the substantial augmentation of resources for overall development of road network.
44.       The Committee is of the view that the construction works  carried out by the Border Roads Organisation in many
 of the States   are not upto the mark.  The Committee, therefore, is of the view that an independent team of experts may
 be appointed to visit some of these areas to submit their reports, specifying steps so that improvements can be made
 with regard to quality construction of such roads. The Committee is also of the view that security aspect should not be
 made a cause of the sub standard construction of such roads.
ROADS IN NORTH EAST REGION                            
45.       The Committee understands that there has been a continual neglect of development of road infrastructure in so
 far as the North-East Region is concerned. The condition of roads/national highways in the region are very miserable
 and due to it the region remains cut off from the rest of the country both economically and socially. The Committee
 observes that  North East region deserve special attention of the Government and the Prime Minister has rightly
 announced that 10% of budget for road sector should be allocated for North East region for development of roads. The
 Committee, therefore, recommends that the Planning Commission/Ministry of Surface Transport should ensure that the
 allocation of 10% in the budget for road sector as decided by them should be allocated to this sector in letter and spirit

 amount allocated under this demand for the year 1999-2000 is Rs. 1051.80 crores against Rs. 571.62 at BE stage and at

th plan outlay for this sector was Rs. 10,258.60 crores against an outlay of Rs. 3425 crores for total 8th five
 year plan period.
 
PORTS
48.       In the 9
th five year plan an outlay of Rs. 8000 crores has been provided for port sector. Out of this Rs. 8000
 crores, the shared extra budgetary resources is Rs. 6000 crores and budgetary support is Rs. 2000 crores. During the
 year 1999-2000 an amount of Rs. 1603.70 crores has been approved against Rs. 914 crores for the year 1998-99.
 
49.       During 1997-98, the first year of 9
th plan, the gross budgetary allocation was Rs. 357.80 crores and the

 handled by the Major ports till the end of 1997-98.

 various areas in the Ports sector for private sector participation and accordingly the Major Port Trusts Act. 1963 has
 been amended to go in for joint venture and that a number of proposals from private parties have already been received.
 These are at various stages of examination and implementation in different ports particularly in Mumbai Port, J.N.P.T.,
 Chennai Port, Murmugao port, Calcutta port and Tuticorin port. Apart from licensing of the existing container terminal,
 the ports have proposed to construct container berths, general/cargo berths and provide necessary equipments for
 handling containers through private capital investment.
 
52.       The Committee was informed that  the ports are expected to   meet their funds requirement for development
 projects out of their internal resources of inter-corporate loans/external aid without budgetary support and they should
 encourage private sector’s participation also.

 the year 1999-2000. The Committee is of the view that outlay for dredging (maintenance) of Haldia Channel should be
 increased or atleast maintained, as per last year’s allocations in view of heavy siltation as Calcutta and Haldia Port are
 reverine ports.

 Scheme for implementation. The Committee desires that an early decision may be taken with regard to this scheme.

SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS
 
ON ROAD TRANSPORT SECTOR
1.         The Committee was very much surprised to know that the budgetary allocation for this important sector relating
 to road transport, which covers matters relating to road safety, control of vehicular pollution, accidents on roads etc.,
 which directly effects public life, has not only been reduced for the year 1998-99 but a lesser amount provided during
 1999=2000. The total 9
th plan allocation is only Rs. 77.15 crores against Rs. 378 crores recommended by the working
 group on road transport sector as compared to Rs. 264 crores during 8th plan. The Committee is of the opinion that
 keeping in view the high rate of accidents on Indian roads and the existing levels of pollution especially in the
 metropolitan cities, this sector deserves higher allocations which would go a long way in making the driving safer on
 the Indian roads as well as for providing clean environment in the cities.
ON ROAD SAFETY MEASURES
2.         The Committee was unhappy to note that despite its recommendation as contained in its 33
rd Report for
 enhanced budgetary allocation for road safety measures, no action appears to have been taken by the Ministry to
 increase the amount for the said purpose and instead only Rs. 1 Crore has been provided whereas Rs. 2.5 crores was the
 budgetary allocation during the year 1998-99.  The Committee further observed that with this meager allocation it
 would not be possible for the Ministry to cover all the States. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its earlier
 recommendation that amount for the purpose should be increased in order to give wide publicity to various road safety
 measures, so that the number of road accidents which are increasing day by day could be reduced.  The Committee
 further recommends that a Centrally sponsored scheme should be introduced for this purpose so that more and more
 States could enjoy the benefits of it in order to make transport system of their States more safer and pollution free.
ON CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS TO S.R.T.C.’S
3.         The Committee desires that reasons for discontinuing the scheme may be furnished to it. However, the
 Committee observed that many States have requested for revival of the scheme, it would be appropriate if such a
 scheme may be revived especially  for the benefit of those States which are totally dependent on road transport. The
 Committee also desires that funds should be provided to those corporations, which could improve their performance if
 financial support is extended to them.
ON INLAND WATER TRANSPORT SECTOR
4.         The Committee was informed that this mode of transport is more cost-effective than road sector. The
 Committee, therefore, recommends that Public Sector Undertakings may be asked to earmark some percentage of their
 Cargo for water transport sector. The Committee, further, recommends that the Ministry should take up the matter with
 regard to less allocation of grants to this sector  with the Planning Commission more seriously and it should be
 specifically underlined to the Planning Commission the significance of this important transport sector,  which would, if
 developed in time, not only lessen the burden on the road/rail sectors but also is a much cleaner and less polluting mode
 of transportation.  They may also be apprised that  the projects under IWT sector are moving at a snail’s pace and in
 order to ensure that these are completed in time without further cost overruns,  it is necessary that adequate allocations
 should be made for water transport sector.  The Committee also observed that in our country the IWT sector has been
 neglected for a long time and if the same attitude continues towards such a nature friendly transportation system,
 definitely the IWT sector will not survive. The Committee also desired that a total review of the IWT sector is required
 and suggests that both the Ministry of Surface Transport and Planning Commission take a realistic view and prepare
 such a plan so as to make a better use of this mode of transportation.
ON CENTRAL INLAND WATER TRANSPORT CORPORATION
5.         The Committee, therefore, impresses upon the Ministry of Surface Transport to take an early decision with
 regard to the restructuring of CIWTC which would also give boost to the growth and development of IWT sector in the
 country.

 Schemes and the constraints in respect of generating funds for implementation of National Highways Schemes. The

 slowly the National Highways are getting converted into intercity highways. The Committee also shows it concern to
